On Tue, Mar 31, 2015 at 11:36 AM, Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org> wrote:
Hi -- can I post this answer to the BioGeoBEARS listserv?

You are correct about the marginal vs. joint estimators and display results -- I'm glad you noticed my comments on this, since it is very common for readers to misinterpret marginal state probabilities at each node as a joint history across all nodes. Unfortunately, I don't have a method for estimating the single best joint history, so that's not an option unless someone develops it. It's probably possible, but then again, even if the joint estimate is done, that exact history is likely to have a tiny probability anyway and might not be representative of the overall probabilities.

As you note, the "problem" (or feature, depending on your point of view) can be worse for some models than others -- e.g. DEC is often a poorer-fitting model, and poorer-fitting models often have a lot of uncertainty at each node/corner, and thus it is not uncommon that, for example, a few lower-probability histories can add up to produce a most-probable state at a corner that appears to conflict with the most-probable state at a node.

Solutions:

1. Look at/use the pie charts.

2. Biogeographical stochastic mapping will produce a sample of histories, each of which will be fully consistent with the specified model. However, the BSM code on the website is still beta, although I'm getting close.

Cheers!
Nick





On Tue, Mar 31, 2015 at 2:06 PM, William Iles <will.j...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello Dr Matzke,

I was looking over results from a BioGeoBears run and I noticed some impossible node-corner results (at least for the DEC model if not the DEC+J model). It seems likely that this is because the output displays marginal instead of joint estimations for ancestral ranges, as you point out online and in your thesis. Since I am interested in particular biogeographic scenarios I was wondering whether it would be possible to plot the best joint estimation of ancestral ranges to guarantee consistent cladogenesis patterns? Or would you recommend against that sort of thing?

Sincerely,
Will
